flagged.title: One God, the Gurus and Sikh Beliefs about Humanity
flagged.reason: The video states that in Sikhism the soul does not dissolve like a drop of water in the ocean, directly contradicting canonical Guru Granth Sahib imagery taught at GCSE where mukti is specifically pictured as water merging into water or light into Light.

mark_affecting.quote: Unlike some traditions, where the soul just sort of dissolves like a drop of water in the ocean, and loses its identity for ever, the Sikh soul continues in a state of active, joyful, loving union and service to God.

flagged.title: Worship in the Gurdwara, Langar and Sikh Initiation
flagged.reason: The video presents the old claim on slide and in voiceover that Guru Granth Sahib page 349 affirms seva and sharing food (langar), which misquotes and misattributes a specification-cited scriptural source on equality.

mark_affecting.quote: affirms the value of seva and the community practice of sharing food together.
prove how langar, seva, and the theological concept of equality are perfectly tied together in Sikh scripture.

flagged.title: Authority, Equality and Sikh Festivals
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly presents 'All humanity is born from the same clay' both on screen and in narration as a direct quotation from Guru Granth Sahib page 349 (a key set text on the GCSE specification).

mark_affecting.quote: Look at this quote from page 349 of the Guru Granth Sahib... It says all humanity is born from the same clay.
